purpose: Optional educational reference in Module 1; qualitative action-potential comparisons, not dosing or treatment selection.

visualConventions.apLabel: Local membrane potential, inside minus outside (mV)
visualConventions.ecgDistinction: An action potential is a voltage across one cell membrane. An ECG lead records a difference between two extracellular electrode potentials.
visualConventions.strengthNotice: The slider exaggerates selected mechanisms for teaching; it is not a drug concentration, dose, or predicted patient response.
visualConventions.modelNotice: Cartoons simplify geometry and motion. Structural evidence identifies a binding site; it does not measure the animated binding trajectory.

quinidineNav.site: Central pore cavity just beneath the selectivity filter; contacts span repeats I, III and IV.
quinidineNav.note: Quinidine both obstructs the pore and changes the intracellular gate. Do not draw every Class I drug in this exact pose.

flecainideNav.note: A rat NaV1.5 construct, not a resolved human-channel complex.

propafenoneNav.note: The fast-inactivation IFM motif was mutated to QQQ to trap an open state; this is not a normal resting channel.

verapamilCav.note: This is an L-type homolog, not the cardiac CaV1.2/CaV1.3 channel. The comparison illustrates a conserved pore-blocking mechanism.

diltiazemCav.note: This is an L-type homolog, not a resolved cardiac CaV1.2 drug complex.

digoxinPump.site: Extracellular-facing cardiotonic-steroid pocket in the transmembrane domain
digoxinPump.note: Show pump inhibition and its downstream calcium consequence separately from vagal slowing of AV conduction.

adenosineA1.site: Extracellular-facing orthosteric pocket of a GPCR
adenosineA1.note: The A1 receptor regulates channels through G proteins; adenosine is not a physical plug in the calcium pore.

hERGReference.note: The channel reference is drug-free. Functional mutagenesis supports a blocker-sensitive pore region, including Y652 and F656, but this does not establish an atomically resolved pose for each listed medicine.

drugs.name: Quinidine
drugs.summary: Slows the fast sodium upstroke and delays repolarization. The two effects can widen conduction time and lengthen QT.
drugs.apEffect: Slower phase 0; longer action potential and refractoriness.
drugs.ecgEffect: Conduction slowing and QT prolongation; nodal and autonomic effects complicate rate changes.

drugs.name: Procainamide
drugs.summary: Reduces fast-tissue conduction and increases refractoriness. Its active metabolite NAPA contributes additional repolarization effects.
drugs.apEffect: Slower phase 0; prolonged refractoriness and repolarization.
drugs.ecgEffect: Can prolong QRS and QT.

drugs.name: Disopyramide
drugs.summary: Reduces fast-cell upstroke velocity and prolongs action-potential duration; it also has antimuscarinic and negative inotropic effects.
drugs.apEffect: Slower phase 0; longer repolarization.
drugs.ecgEffect: QT may lengthen; the size of QRS changes depends on exposure and tissue.

drugs.name: Lidocaine
drugs.summary: Blocks sodium current with rapid recovery from block. Its effects depend on channel state and tissue conditions.
drugs.apEffect: Usually little change in normal fast-tissue conduction at therapeutic exposure; shorter ventricular/Purkinje action potentials.
drugs.ecgEffect: Usually little QRS or QT change in otherwise normal tissue.

drugs.name: Mexiletine
drugs.summary: An orally active sodium-current blocker with lidocaine-like electrophysiology; reducing inward sodium current can shorten repolarization.
drugs.apEffect: Modest upstroke effect in normal tissue; shorter action-potential duration in susceptible preparations.
drugs.ecgEffect: Often little effect on normal QRS; QT shortening is context dependent.

drugs.name: Flecainide
drugs.summary: Strong sodium-current block slows fast conduction, especially through His-Purkinje tissue. Block accumulates with repeated activation.
drugs.apEffect: Markedly slower phase 0; action-potential duration is not the main teaching effect.
drugs.ecgEffect: QRS and PR can lengthen; a longer QT may partly reflect the wider QRS.

drugs.name: Propafenone
drugs.summary: Blocks the open sodium pore and slows the fast upstroke. Additional beta-blocking effects influence nodal behavior.
drugs.apEffect: Slower phase 0 with use-dependent conduction slowing.
drugs.ecgEffect: QRS and PR can lengthen.

drugs.name: Esmolol
drugs.summary: Short-acting, preferential beta1-receptor antagonism reduces sympathetic acceleration of pacemaker and AV nodal tissue.
drugs.apEffect: Reduced phase-4 acceleration under sympathetic drive; slower nodal pacing and AV conduction.
drugs.ecgEffect: Longer RR and often PR; no obligatory direct QRS widening.

drugs.name: Metoprolol
drugs.summary: Preferential beta1-receptor antagonism reduces catecholamine signaling. Channel effects are downstream of the receptor.
drugs.apEffect: Slower pacemaker depolarization under sympathetic drive; slower AV conduction.
drugs.ecgEffect: Longer RR and often PR.

drugs.name: Atenolol
drugs.summary: Preferential beta1-receptor antagonism blunts sympathetic cardiac stimulation; selectivity is not absolute.
drugs.apEffect: Reduced sympathetic acceleration of nodal phase 4.
drugs.ecgEffect: Longer RR and potentially PR.

drugs.name: Propranolol
drugs.summary: Nonselective beta-receptor antagonism reduces catecholamine responses. Its high-concentration membrane effects are not the principal illustration.
drugs.apEffect: Less sympathetic acceleration of nodal pacing and conduction.
drugs.ecgEffect: Longer RR and potentially PR.

drugs.name: Dofetilide
drugs.summary: Blocks the rapid delayed-rectifier potassium current, reducing outward current during repolarization.
drugs.apEffect: Longer action potential and effective refractory period with little direct fast-upstroke effect.
drugs.ecgEffect: QT prolongation.

drugs.name: Sotalol
drugs.summary: Combines repolarization prolongation with nonselective beta blockade. Both effects matter.
drugs.apEffect: Longer ventricular action potential plus slower nodal pacing and conduction.
drugs.ecgEffect: QT and RR lengthen; PR can lengthen.

drugs.name: Amiodarone
drugs.summary: Has effects spanning all four Vaughan Williams classes. Chronic exposure prolongs repolarization; acute and chronic effects differ.
drugs.apEffect: Longer repolarization, rate-dependent sodium effects, and slower nodal activity.
drugs.ecgEffect: QT and PR may lengthen; effects are not reproduced by a single-channel plug.

drugs.name: Dronedarone
drugs.summary: Has activities in all four antiarrhythmic classes. The contribution of each activity to its clinical effect remains uncertain.
drugs.apEffect: Illustrate mixed nodal and repolarization changes, without asserting a unique molecular mechanism.
drugs.ecgEffect: PR and QTc can lengthen.

drugs.name: Ibutilide
drugs.summary: Prolongs repolarization. The prescribing information emphasizes activation of a slow inward, predominantly sodium current, so it should not be shown as a pure potassium blocker.
drugs.apEffect: Longer action potential and refractoriness.
drugs.ecgEffect: QT lengthens with little direct QRS effect.

drugs.name: Verapamil
drugs.summary: Reduces L-type calcium influx. AV nodal upstrokes depend on calcium current, making nodal conduction a key teaching target.
drugs.apEffect: Slower calcium-dependent nodal phase 0 and greater AV nodal refractoriness.
drugs.ecgEffect: PR can lengthen; normal intraventricular conduction is not the principal target.

drugs.name: Diltiazem
drugs.summary: Reduces L-type calcium influx and slows AV nodal conduction. Its use-dependent nodal effect is especially relevant during rapid rhythms.
drugs.apEffect: Slower calcium-dependent phase 0 and prolonged AV nodal refractoriness.
drugs.ecgEffect: PR lengthens; little direct effect on normal sodium-dependent ventricular conduction.

drugs.name: Adenosine
drugs.summary: Activates the A1 receptor, which couples to Gi. Downstream potassium-current activation and reduced calcium signaling transiently suppress AV nodal conduction.
drugs.apEffect: Hyperpolarization and slower or temporarily absent nodal excitation.
drugs.ecgEffect: Transient AV conduction interruption; atrial activity can continue during the pause.

drugs.name: Digoxin
drugs.summary: Inhibits the sodium-potassium pump, altering intracellular sodium and calcium handling. Its AV nodal slowing also involves increased parasympathetic influence.
drugs.apEffect: Separate vagal nodal slowing from increased calcium availability; excess calcium can promote triggered activity.
drugs.ecgEffect: Slower AV conduction and characteristic ST-T effects are not a simple class-III QT change.

drugs.name: Magnesium
drugs.summary: Modifies several ionic processes. Experimental magnesium administration can suppress early afterdepolarizations; there is no single validated antiarrhythmic binding pose to display.
drugs.apEffect: Show a smaller triggered oscillation on a prolonged action potential; do not automatically normalize QT.
drugs.ecgEffect: Suppression of triggered activity does not require a proportional shortening of QT.
